name: Trans Am
label: Thrill Jockey
lede: Three friends from suburban Maryland who fired their singer, plugged in a Casio, named themselves after a muscle car, and spent thirty years poking post-rock in the ribs with vocoders and Van Halen.

eras.title: A band across three campuses
eras.text: Nathan Means, Philip Manley and Sebastian Thomson grew up around North Bethesda, Maryland, and started Trans Am while at three different colleges. They came up in the shadow of Fugazi and Bad Brains, and never quite fit the D.C. scene.

years.h: Trans Am starts as a long-distance band
years.p: Means at UNC Chapel Hill, Manley at Oberlin and Thomson at Bard form a band across three campuses, rehearsing when they can and moving to Maryland after graduating.
years.xp: Manley later said living in the same place turned out to be much harder than the long-distance setup they started with.

q: Fuck a Corvette. We should call it Trans Am.
years.h: Philip Manley wants Corvette; Sebastian Thomson wants Trans Am
years.p: Manley pitches Corvette as the band's name. Thomson shoots it down in favor of the Pontiac, and the car wins.
years.xp: Thomson told the story to Phoenix New Times in 2014, on the band's twentieth-plus year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Trans Am (band) · Phoenix New Times (2014)
years.h: Trans Am kicks out its singer for skipping rehearsal
years.p: A friend on vocals keeps not showing up, so the band fires him and never replaces him. Trans Am becomes an instrumental band by accident.
years.xp: Thomson told Phoenix New Times the singer, a friend, would never show up for rehearsal, so they kicked him out.

years.src: Wikipedia: Trans Am (band) · The Skinny (2014) · Tokafi (2012)
years.h: A Casio keyboard turns Trans Am from hardcore kids into something else
years.p: In North Carolina around 1993, the band plugs in a cheap Casio and decides a keyboard can be a punk instrument too. Out go the D.C. models; in come Kraftwerk, Aphex Twin and Autechre.
years.xp: The band's early touchstones were [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]], [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]] and [[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]]. After the Casio, the list became Chrome, This Heat, Van Halen, Manowar, Kraftwerk, Aphex Twin and Autechre. Manley has said Trans Am owes more to Kraftwerk and early electronica than to krautrock.

q: The D.C. scene was very self-serious and very political.
years.h: The D.C. scene that left Trans Am out
years.p: Trans Am came from the D.C. suburbs but felt shut out of the hardcore scene. Manley found it self-serious and political; Means notes the band is missing from scene histories despite a big national profile.
years.xp: Thomson told The Skinny the band was always a little left out, partly because it wanted to have fun. Means told Phoenix New Times that Trans Am had a bigger national profile than all but a few D.C. bands and still got left out of the story.

eras.title: Tortoise's opening act, with Moogs
eras.text: Thrill Jockey signed them, John McEntire produced them, and Tortoise took them on the road. Critics filed Trans Am under post-rock; the band kept adding synths and arena-rock guitar until it started singing through a vocoder.

years.h: Trans Am · a McEntire production in a space-kit sleeve
years.p: The 30-minute debut, recorded at Idful in Chicago, comes out the same day as Tortoise's Millions Now Living Will Never Die. Its cover reuses art from a 1980 National Geographic flexi disc called Space Sounds.
years.xp: Guitar Player heard a musicianly spacerock meltdown full of Moog blasts; AllMusic's Sean Cooper found it enjoyable but somewhat expendable. Some guitar parts drew comparisons to Foreigner and Boston.

years.h: Trans Am opens for Tortoise across the US
years.p: After McEntire produces the debut, Trans Am goes on a US tour supporting [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]].

years.h: Starjammer ends up on a Gilles Deleuze tribute
years.p: A split single with [[Wingtip Sloat|949a298b-bd56-493d-ad2c-65aa54fc266e]] on Tuba Frenzy carries Starjammer, which the German label Mille Plateaux later puts on In Memoriam Gilles Deleuze.

years.h: Surrender to the Night · one year to the day later
years.p: Trans Am's second album comes out exactly a year after the first, again with McEntire. Entertainment Weekly hears Wire-esque jaggedness, arena-rock machismo and dance beats.
years.xp: The Washington Post called it a band pushing all the dance, noise and punk envelopes. The longest track, Carboforce, runs almost eight minutes.

years.h: The Surveillance · the third album
years.p: Trans Am's third Thrill Jockey album in three years.

years.h: Futureworld: Trans Am starts singing, through a vocoder
years.p: On its fourth album the instrumental band adds lyrics for the first time, all run through vocoders. The Village Voice calls it the band's definitive futurist new wave statement.
years.xp: The band produced it themselves. Pitchfork gave it 8.0; Trouser Press thought the robot singing took a back seat to grooves that nearly imprison the songs.

eras.title: Pranksters in the machine
eras.text: With their own studio in D.C., Trans Am made a 73-minute double album, then a synth-pop record critics took as a joke and a political one aimed at the Bush White House. The band has said the jokes were never only jokes.

years.h: Red Line · 24 tracks and the Windows 98 startup sound
years.p: The 73-minute double album, made at Trans Am's own National Recording Studio, time-stretches the Windows 98 startup chime into Let's Take the Fresh Step Together. [[Ian Svenonius|0ef9be87-0dbe-4551-a526-f3f6891a2e9d]] guests on Ragged Agenda.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 8.7. The New York Times said the band had finally embraced free-form rock with a beat, and Trouser Press called it a sprawling career summary of the band's obsessions.

years.h: You Can Always Get What You Want: the rarities
years.p: Trans Am gathers its odds and ends and non-album tracks on one Thrill Jockey collection.

years.src: Wikipedia: TA (album) · Wikipedia: Trans Am (band) · The Skinny (2014)
years.h: TA goes synth-pop and Pitchfork gives it 3.5
years.p: Trans Am's sixth album, co-produced with McEntire, swerves into slick synthetic pop. Critics read it as parody; Sebastian Thomson says it was a reaction against post-rock's seriousness, not a joke.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the record as parodying REO Speedwagon's look and says it was mostly panned. Thomson told The Skinny in 2014 that critics often misread it.

years.h: Liberation · Trans Am takes on the Bush years
years.p: The seventh album is about George W. Bush's presidency, the 2003 invasion of Iraq, the war on terror and propaganda.

eras.title: Opening for Tool
eras.text: Trans Am took its analog synths into arenas in front of Tool fans, soundtracked a PlayStation Portable game and put out sixteen years of live tapes. It was still on Thrill Jockey, fifteen years into the label.

years.h: Sex Change · the eighth album
years.p: A US tour with [[Zombi|aa3dbea9-a183-42d4-8b30-a894d1fa3844]] and [[The Psychic Paramount|5f9a7c33-f744-4749-beb1-4e8ed69edd37]] follows. Pitchfork gives it 7.0.

years.h: Trans Am plays seventeen shows opening for Tool
years.p: The Maryland trio spends seventeen nights warming up arena crowds for [[Tool|66fc5bf8-daa4-4241-b378-9bc9077939d2]], the biggest stages of its career.

years.h: Thrill Jockey turns 15 and Trans Am plays the party
years.p: The band performs at the label's 15th anniversary show in Chicago and scores the PSP game After Burner: Black Falcon.

years.h: What Day Is It Tonight?: live, 1993–2008
years.p: A live compilation spanning fifteen years, limited to 1,500 copies.

years.h: Thing · the ninth album
years.p: Trans Am's ninth studio album on Thrill Jockey.

eras.title: Three cities, one consensus
eras.text: By the 2010s Thomson lived in Brooklyn, Manley in the Bay Area and Means in Portland, and Thomson had a second job drumming for Baroness. The band met up when it could and kept making records by consensus.

years.h: Sebastian Thomson joins Baroness
years.p: The Savannah metal band hires Thomson after its drummer retires following the band's bus accident. He plays on Purple, Gold & Grey and Stone.

years.h: Volume X · album ten
years.p: Thomson tells The Skinny the secret to lasting is simple: they still like each other, and they don't live in the same city.

years.h: Election night interrupts the California Hotel sessions
years.p: Trans Am is recording in San Francisco when the 2016 result comes in, and Thrill Jockey says the band worked that night into the album.

years.src: Bandcamp Daily (2017) · Thrill Jockey: Trans Am
years.h: California Hotel: named for an Oakland hotel, and the Eagles
years.p: Recorded live at El Studio in San Francisco over four one-week sessions in two years, the album is named for a hotel Philip Manley saw off I-580 in Oakland. Thrill Jockey says it also honors the late Glenn Frey.
years.xp: Manley told Bandcamp Daily the hotel name was just stupid enough to be a Trans Am title, and admitted he used to hate the Eagles himself. Vintage Moog, Micro-Korg and Crumar synths are all over it.

years.h: Sebastian Thomson sits in on Late Night with Seth Meyers
years.p: Trans Am's drummer spends a week, May 20 to 23, as guest drummer for the NBC show's band.
